title: Character Animation in a 2D Game
author: Single-Control5624
selftext:
**Character Animation in a 2D Game**

Hi everyone!

I'm developing a game using AI tools (obviously!), and I'm struggling to find a good workflow for character animation.

My game is 2D, and I've been generating my characters using OpenAI. I'm really happy with the designs, so I'd like to preserve their original appearance as much as possible. The problem is figuring out how to animate them properly.

For the enemies, I converted the 2D designs into 3D models, rendered them, and brought them back into 2D. This allowed me to create skeletons in Godot and get them moving.

However, doing the same thing with human characters has been much more challenging because AI seems to struggle with understanding and reproducing natural human movement.

When I tried generating 2D animations directly, the AI split the images into hundreds of pieces and attempted to animate them frame by frame. The result looked more like a puppet than a proper animated character.

I also tried converting the human characters to 3D and rendering them back into 2D, but this caused them to lose their original designs, which is something I'd really like to avoid.

My goal is to achieve a style of animation similar to *Hero Wars*. I'm not looking for anything particularly complex, just smooth, appealing character animations that work well in a 2D mobile game.

I'm currently using Godot for development, along with OpenAI, Magnific, Claude, and other AI tools.

**What workflow would you recommend for this situation?** Is there a reliable way to animate AI-generated human characters while preserving their original designs? Would you recommend 2D skeletal animation, 3D rendering, AI-assisted animation tools, or something else entirely?

I'd really appreciate any suggestions, especially from people who have dealt with similar challenges in AI-assisted game development.

Thanks!

comments.author: UnfortunateHurricane
comments.body:
>>  Is there a reliable way to animate AI-generated human characters while preserving their original designs? Would you recommend 2D skeletal animation, 3D rendering, AI-assisted animation tools, or something else entirely?

Somewhat.

There have been a few sprite sheet generators around here. You can run them locally if you have a good GPU. Most of them use Minimax H3 as the video model and then pick the best few frames for an action.

I also wrote a wrapper for that which helps it to be a bit more organized. It assumes a running comfyui instance. You can find it in my recent posts.

Then there are some paid versions doing the same / similar.
Just yesterday was a big post from the Autosprite dev. There is also Pixellab. I am neither affiliated nor have used any of them. Just know they exist. You might want to look in them.
